messages:
maria: FYI production SSO errors started 09:12 UTC. Saw a bunch of 401s with "Audience mismatch". Correlation ID: cor-9f3a1c. Sample log:
```
saml: assertion validation failed: audience mismatch: expected=https://redwood.example.com/, got=https://app.example.com/
relay_state=... 
```

jamal: ack, on it. any recent RBAC or metadata pushes?

maria: pushed nothing. Last metadata refresh from Okta was 09:00; idp metadata looks unchanged.

alex: @rin can you grab the SP metadata in our vault? maybe our entityID changed in latest canary.

rin: pulling from vault now. Looks like sp.entity_id is "https://redwood-internal/" in /secrets/sso/sp-metadata.json — that doesn't match host header. hmm.

deploy-bot: deploy redwood-api canary finished 08:57 by @infra-oncall

infra-oncall: I rotated a hostname alias yesterday for internal routing; could've changed ACS url. Rolling back? :eyes:

maria: stop - don't rollback yet. We need to confirm customers. One customer is seeing sign-in loop + SCIM provision fail: "externalId required". Logs show KMS decrypt error before mapping:

```
kms: decrypt failed: InvalidEnvelopeError: tag mismatch
trace=corr=cor-9f3a1c
```

jamal: tag mismatch usually means ciphertext format changed or key alias mismatch. Did we rotate the KMS alias yesterday? @infra-oncall

infra-oncall: yes we rotated alias redwood-sso-key -> redwood-sso-key-v2 at 02:00 UTC; we updated services that use envelope tags but maybe not the SCIM worker.

alex: quick triage steps: 1) confirm idp entityID + ACS exactly match SP metadata 2) verify KMS alias used by scim-provisioner 3) check clock skew <5s 4) dump full SAML assertion (safe masked) to find externalId attr.

rin: ran `kubectl -n prod exec scim-provisioner -- curl http://localhost:8080/health` -> OK. Config shows KMS_ALIAS=redwood-sso-key-v2 but env var masked in pod; need to check mounted secret version.

maria: I can pull the assertion for the failing user. Assertion shows:
```
<NameID Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress">user@customer.com</NameID>
<Attribute Name="externalId">12345</Attribute>
<AudienceRestriction><Audience>https://app.example.com/</Audience></AudienceRestriction>
```

jamal: that's the "got" audience. Our SP expects https://redwood.example.com/ — where's the rewrite? maybe reverse proxy changed host header to app.example.com.

alex: confirm proxy change: infra-oncall?

infra-oncall: yes we have an ingress rule rewrite: host header preserved -> app.example.com for that host. We can add host alias in SP metadata to accept both audiences.

maria: adding secondary audience is ok short-term, but KMS decrypt still failing for SCIM mapping — could be different code path using different key version. We need urgent fix: mark incident P1, notify SOC.

jamal: opening incident -> INC-2026-042. I'm adding runbook steps.

rin: temp fix: set scim-provisioner KMS_ALIAS back to redwood-sso-key for that deployment and restart pod. Doing now.

deploy-bot: restart scim-provisioner pod triggered by @rin

maria: after restart, SCIM provisioning succeeded for the test user. SAML login still fails for some clients due to audience.

alex: plan: 1) update SP metadata to include both https://redwood.example.com/ and https://app.example.com/ 2) coordinate with infra to stop host rewrite or add rewrite to preserve original host header 3) rotate KMS envelope properly and roll scim-provisioner 4) add monitoring alert for KMS tag mismatch

rin: I'll prepare metadata patch and PR for both. Also adding an eval to check SAML audience mismatch logs.

jamal: also add audit log entry for the KMS rotation change and which services updated (for compliance).

maria: thanks. tagging @security-legal for audit note. :thumbsup:

infra-oncall: follow-up: we will schedule a non-breaking alias for host rewrite and doc the impact.

maria: closing loop — for now set incident to P1 but we de-escalate after KMS and metadata patched. last tested 09:28 UTC.
